# Blackline 0.15.42

The rest of Derek's list of 18 September, in one package. (0.15.41 was built and then folded into
this one: a source edit landed mid-build, so its contents no longer matched its notes, and a package
whose contents cannot be described is not worth shipping.)

## The floating call card, rebuilt

It only comes up when there is a picture to carry — a screen share or a camera. A voice call with
nothing to see does not get one; the way back to that call is the voice panel in the sidebar, which
is up the whole time the call is.

When there *is* a picture and you have put it down, the card stays and offers it back rather than
vanishing — a share that started while you were elsewhere is worth knowing about. Put down, it draws
the person instead of the picture, dimmed, with one button in front and a line saying whose picture
is waiting. Nothing of theirs is drawn while it is down.

Right-clicking gives **Stop watching** / **Watch the stream**, **Open the call**, **Leave the call**.
The right button opens that menu instead of dragging the card.

The card itself: a real shadow with a wide soft pass and a tight contact one, a hairline that
lightens as the pointer arrives, a lift while dragging, LIVE moved off the buttons to the top left,
and the bar rising from the bottom edge rather than appearing on top of it.

## Settings to a file and back

**Settings → Settings file.** Everything chosen in settings written to one file and read back from
one. The pane says plainly what it is not: no keys, no identity, no contacts, no messages — loading
it onto another device does not make that device you. Loading asks first, says how many settings the
file carries and when it was saved, and refuses a file that is not a Blackline settings file rather
than half-applying it.

## Roles

Right-clicking a role gives **Duplicate role**, **View the space as this role**, **Copy role ID** and
**Delete role**, each greyed with a reason when your own roles do not reach. Duplicate copies the
colour, the hoist and every grant and names it "X copy". *View as* answers "what would somebody
holding only this hold?" from the record already on this device — nothing is changed and nobody is
told, and a bar says so until you leave it. Delete says how many members hold it before you agree.

## Invites

How long one lasts (30 minutes to 30 days) and how many people it lets in (1, 5, 25, or no limit) are
now chosen when it is made. Every invite this device is still honouring is listed with what is left
of it and a button to stop it. The lifetime is capped at 30 days rather than offering "never": an
invite that never expires is one nobody remembers handing out.

**Not shortened, deliberately.** Everything needed to reach you and check your keys is inside the
invite, which is what lets joining ask nothing of anybody else. A short code has to be looked up
somewhere, and the only place Blackline has is the name registry — which would mean invites only
worked for people who have claimed a username, and would publish that the space exists. That trade
may be worth making; it is not made without asking.

## Adding people to a conversation

A direct conversation has an add-people button in its header. It opens the group sheet with that
person already chosen. **If you are in a call with them, the call moves into the new room's voice**
rather than dropping.

## Permissions

Seven new ones, each with its own row and its own honest class mark:

| | What it does | Class |
|---|---|---|
| **See who people are** | Anything past the name and picture somebody shows here — the account name behind a nickname, their handle, their status, their devices | 2 |
| **Approve who joins** | Take part in gating who gets in | 2 |
| **Pin messages** | Pin, without being able to delete anyone's | 2 |
| **Read message history** | Read what was said before you arrived | 2 |
| **Send voice messages** | Record and send one | 2 |
| **Move members** | Move somebody between voice channels, or out of voice | 3 |
| **Lock voice channels** | Close a channel's voice; whoever is in stays | 2 |

**Reactions, @everyone, mute, deafen and your profile in a space were already permissions** and are
unchanged — they are in the same list.

**Taking channels away from people already exists and is stronger than a permission.** A channel with
readers has its own key, sealed to those roles: a member who is not a reader holds nothing that opens
it and does not see the channel at all. That is Class 1 — it holds against a modified client, which
no permission does.

### One correction, stated plainly

I first wrote **See who people are** as Class 1 — claiming the space would stop carrying those
fields. It will not, and I corrected it before building. A space's member records are replicated to
every member so that anyone can verify anyone, so those fields are already on every member's device;
hiding them is honest software honouring a rule, which is Class 2. Making it Class 1 means sealing
the fields to a role's key the way a private channel's words are sealed to its readers. That is
possible and it is not built.

## Voice channels

**How many at once** is now a setting per channel, and it is not capped at eight. The field says what
the number means: a mesh call is one connection per person and this device carries about eight, so a
limit above that is a rule about who may walk in, not a promise about what the hardware will do.

**Voice is closed** shuts a channel to anybody not already in it. Whoever is in stays. It needs the
lock-voice permission, checked in the core and not only in the interface.

Walking into a channel whose voice is shut, or full, now says which it is.

## Still to come from the list

- **Join requests** — gating a private space and approving the people who ask. The permission is in;
  the request itself is a protocol addition and is next.
- **The members management page** — the table with selection and bulk actions.

Both were held back rather than half-built.
